calls.head: Suzuki gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Rangers keep sending Miller’s line (Kartye, Miller and Dorofeyev) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Sullivan has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Canadiens’ first line is Caufield, Suzuki and Slafkovský.

surprises.head: The Rangers shut down Montréal’s power play
surprises.body: Montréal’s power play created 1.6 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.3 and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Cuylle has two goals as the Rangers take down the Canadiens
paras: Phillip Danault got the scoring started for the Canadiens early in the second, but Will Cuylle made it 1-1 for the Rangers less than two minutes later. Cuylle scored again shorthanded with just under a minute left in the period to put the Rangers ahead for good. Scott Morrow made it 3-1 early in the third.
The Canadiens had a little more of the play, but the Rangers had the finish. Joonas Korpisalo made 24 saves for the Rangers, and Jacob Fowler stopped 23 of 26 at the other end.

Neither power play scored: the Rangers killed all four Canadiens power plays, and the Canadiens killed all three of the Rangers’. The Rangers improved to 13-8-1, third in the Metropolitan, while the Habs dropped to 12-5-4, slipping to third in the Atlantic.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Rangers.
Mika Zibanejad’s eight-game point streak against Montréal ended.
Adam Fox extended his point streak against Montréal to nine games.
With Pavel Dorofeyev out, Cuylle took his spot and scored twice.
